name: Hotel Daspalla — Dharani
signature_dish: Andhra vegetarian thali — the value-for-money meal Vizag locals send outsiders to
why_it_matters: Hotel Daspalla's Suryabagh property is one of the oldest hospitality addresses in central Vizag, and its Dharani veg restaurant is the answer most locals give when asked where to get a proper Andhra meal in the city centre. The thali is the order — multiple curries, two rices, rasam, and gongura on a single plate at a price point a tourist hotel rarely matches.
insider_tip: Go for the lunch thali rather than à la carte — it is the same kitchen and far better value. The non-veg sister restaurant Dakshin in the same complex handles seafood and Andhra meat dishes; ask reception which one is serving if you arrive between sittings.
signature_address: Hotel Daspalla, Town Main Road, Suryabagh, near Jagadamba Theatre, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh 530020

name: Dakshin (Hotel Daspalla)
signature_dish: Andhra-style non-veg buffet — coastal fish curry, prawn and crab fry
why_it_matters: Dakshin is Hotel Daspalla's Andhra non-vegetarian restaurant — the city-centre spot for coastal Andhra seafood without going out to a beach-road shack. The South-Indian non-veg buffet at lunch and dinner is the easiest way for a first-timer to graze across prawn iguru, fish fry and crab in one sitting.
insider_tip: Buffet beats à la carte here for variety. Bommidayala pulusu (smelt-fish curry) is the dish that marks this out as genuine coastal Andhra rather than generic South Indian — ask if it is on that day.
signature_address: Dakshin, Hotel Daspalla premises, Town Main Road, Suryabagh, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh 530020

name: Sea Inn (Raju Gaari Dhaba)
signature_dish: Andhra-spiced crab and prawn fry with biryani, by the Rushikonda sea
why_it_matters: A 20-year-old mom-and-pop seafood shack below Rushikonda hill on the Vizag–Bhimili road — Mr and Mrs K.V. Raju run it (she cooks, he manages). It trades under both 'Sea Inn' and 'Raju Gaari Dhaba'; they are the same place. The crab fry and biryani are the reason it stays crowded despite being a basic open-air mess rather than a fine-dining room.
insider_tip: Expect a 30-60 minute wait at peak meal times — it is small and busy. The food is genuinely Andhra-spicy; ask the kitchen to dial down chilli if you are not used to it. Pair with a Rushikonda beach walk before or after.
signature_address: Sea Inn / Raju Gaari Dhaba, opposite Cyclone Shelter, near GITAM College, Rushikonda, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh 530045

name: Subbayya Gari Hotel
area: Dwaraka Nagar 5th Lane, near Diamond Park
signature_dish: Butta bhojanam — 30-plus-dish unlimited Andhra thali on a banana leaf
why_it_matters: The Vizag branch of the Kakinada-founded Subbayya Gari Hotel — opened here in 2019 and now the city's reference for a full Andhra vegetarian banana-leaf meal. The thali runs to 30-plus items including three rices, seven or eight curries and three sweets, served on a banana leaf with old-style hospitality at a price most tourist restaurants cannot match.
insider_tip: It is unlimited — pace yourself, the servers keep refilling. Lunch is when the full spread is on; arrive by 1pm to avoid the longest waits. Pure-veg only, no alcohol.
signature_address: Savitri Summit, 47-3-12, Dwaraka Nagar 5th Lane, near Diamond Park, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh 530016

name: Sri Sairam Parlour
signature_dish: South Indian tiffin — idli, dosa and vada with peanut chutney
why_it_matters: A pocket-friendly Telugu tiffin house at Asilmetta Junction (with a Dwaraka Nagar sibling) doing the everyday Vizag breakfast — idli, dosa, vada, punugulu — plus a cheap unlimited veg meal at lunch. The peanut chutney is the detail regulars come back for.
insider_tip: Order tiffin in the morning and the unlimited veg thali at lunch — both are among the cheapest honest meals in central Vizag. Seating is basic and it gets crowded at peak; takeaway is quick.
signature_address: 10-1-19/A, Asilmetta Junction, Asilmetta, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh 530003

name: Sri Bramaramba Banana Leaf Hotel
why_it_matters: An old-style banana-leaf meals house near Asilmetta Junction — the kind of no-frills Andhra mess where a working-day lunch is served fast, fresh and unlimited on a leaf. It is the budget counterpart to Daspalla's thali for travellers staying near the RTC Complex / Asilmetta side of the city.
insider_tip: Lunch is the meal here — the leaf meal is when the kitchen is at its best. Plain, fast and cheap; not a place to linger, but an honest Andhra plate.
signature_address: Asilmetta Junction, Asilmetta, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh 530003

name: Zamindari — Royal South Cuisine
signature_dish: Telugu-named royal Andhra dishes served in copper-finish ware
why_it_matters: A theme restaurant in Maharani Peta that recreates the Andhra zamindari era — havildar statues, blue doors, copper-finish serving ware — but the menu keeps real Telugu dish names and coastal Andhra cooking rather than playing dress-up. It is the city's most atmospheric way to eat regional food, good for both veg and non-veg tables.
insider_tip: Book ahead on weekends — it draws a crowd for the decor alone. Order dishes by their Telugu names off the menu; the kitchen leans into authenticity rather than tourist-mild versions.
signature_address: Port Officers Quarters, near Nowroji Road, Maharani Peta, Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh 530002
